notes: Each candidate, hint level, and no-hint discovery stops at its first independently evidenced exploit, so attempt counts give no unbiased success-rate estimate. Not found means not found within the actual attempts. Only the attack inspector's attribution to a check of the same episode confirms the candidate under test; an unrelated or unattributed exploit does not.

An evidenced finding is accepted_invalid (violating work received more than its deserved score) or rejected_valid (valid work received less than it deserved). A finding with open conditions is still evidenced; its open conditions are listed beside it. A legitimate finding has a reward equal to its deserved score and no open condition, which does not judge the work. An inconclusive finding established no outcome, or is legitimate with an open condition. Package findings come from an Inspector sandbox running a copy of the task package, native findings from a task episode. An earlier reading of a check stays listed, marked with the later reading that superseded it. Category settlement and the evidenced count read the latest reading of each check; local labels and metrics read every reading.

A category is evidenced_issue once one of its cases is evidenced (for the hack inspector, an accepted_invalid case), and a later reading does not withdraw it. It is no_evidenced_issue only when a focused attempt completed it after any failure on it, none of its probes was skipped or repeated, its applicability evidence is applicable, at least one case measured in it before the episode sessions has a consistent latest reading, and the latest reading of every such case is consistent with its reward or evidenced; otherwise it stays unknown. A positive reward on a reading with any violated requirement is not consistent, even as correct partial credit. With no focused attempts, no category is no_evidenced_issue. A case belongs to the category of its experiment. A hack inspector case outside the requested categories keeps its own family, or `other` when none fits, and leaves the requested categories alone; an open grader inspector case without an inspected category keeps every category open. A repair, which interprets an ordinary check again in a later session, evidences the category of that session. The Inspector's applicability text is in the JSON report.
